opening: In Maharashtra, housing society committees are unpaid volunteers who sign for crores, and registrars dissolve committees that cannot show a recorded resolution. Apps like MyGate log who approved a payment. Society Room makes sure they had the right to: an invoice, a quorate vote by name, and the bye-law limit. Rules are enforced by Switch roles and deterministic code, not by a prompt. First buyer: the society's auditor, who signs off on exactly these records.
b1: One template creates both rooms and four agents.
b2: A resident says 'just pay it'. Switch itself stops the message: the agent never sees it. Even the Treasurer is refused: no resolution.
b3: The Chairman opens the meeting; the clerk counts quorum, 20 needed, 41 present, and records the vote by name. Only now does the treasurer book: invoice, resolution and bye-law check, all three.
b4: A Rs 4 lakh repainting bid is over the bye-law 156 limit for a society this size. It cannot be approved by the committee, even with a vote. It goes to the General Body agenda.
b5: In the General Body room a resident asks why the society paid the lift contractor. The concierge answers only from the published ledger and minutes, and cites them.
closing: Switch decides who may instruct; the engine decides what is allowed. Same ledger the auditor signs.
